note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM F, team 1905127: a search-and-matching model of a dual monetary system, a national
tax-revenue model, an improved-OCA trade model, and two algebraic regressions of Bitcoin demand
across 53 countries. Twenty-six pages, ten of which carry art, twelve measured regions.

**All twelve are accounted**: 3 native tables, 6 figure rows (5 numbered figures and 1
uncaptioned appendix plate), and 3 refusals. The refusals are the two prose columns the layout
pass measured on p4 and Table 1's own continuation on p6, which belongs to the p5 row through
its `continued` flag rather than to a second table.

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 1.3 "Overview of Our Work" takes **Figure 1**, the roadmap bubble, immediately under the
  paragraph that sets up the whole paper.
- 2.2 "Variable Description" takes **Table 1**, directly under the heading, announced by
  nothing.
- 3.1.2.2 "Equilibrium State of the Model" takes **Figure 2**, the matching triangle, above the
  equations it depicts.
- 4.1.2 "Parameter Estimation and Result Solution" takes **Table 2**; 4.1.3 takes **Table 3**;
  4.1.4 takes **Figure 3**, the choropleth of the 130-country result.
- 4.2 "Empirical Study Based on Macro-model" takes **Figures 4 and 5**, the two simulation
  traces.
- The appendix takes the **p25 fit plate**, printed under the list item "1.Total Trade Volume of
  the United State" and above the code that drew it.

One exhibit per subsection, and never two in the same subsection: the paper hangs each object
from exactly the paragraph that needs it and moves on.

## When it goes 3-D

**Never.** Twelve measured regions, zero perspective, zero surface, zero isometric projection,
no colourbar anywhere. The only depth cue in the file is a stacking of dotted connector weights
in Figure 1, which is emphasis, not a third axis. When this team needs a third variable they
panel it (three traces in Figures 4 and 5, four fill classes in Figure 3) rather than rotate
it.

## What the figures do

| group | count | what it actually is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Figure 1 | 1 | bubble roadmap: 1 centre, 4 displaced themes, 3 scales, 13 italic annotations |
| Figure 2 | 1 | four-box matching triangle with the four transition probabilities as edge labels |
| Figure 3 | 1 | world choropleth, 4-class categorical fill, legend inside over the Pacific |
| Figures 4, 5 | 2 | 3-trace line charts of one simulation, same template, relabelled legend |
| p25 plate | 1 | uncaptioned scatter + linear fit, MATLAB output |
| Tables 1-3 | 3 | parameter list, estimation roster, OLS console |

The three drawings (1, 2, 3) all encode **category, not magnitude**: box position, box
presence, and fill colour. The three charts (4, 5, p25) all encode **time on the x-axis** and
are the only objects with numeric scales. There is no bar, no histogram, no box plot, no
heatmap, no surface anywhere in the file.

## Table shapes worth reusing

| table | shape | trick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table 1 parameter list | 7x2 on p5, 11 more rows on p6 | booktabs, header printed once, no repeated header on the overflow |
| Table 2 estimation roster | 8x2 | the file's only zebra: grey bands shading the rows that form one group |
| Table 3 OLS console | 4x9 | one merged summary band carrying 'Observations 53' and 'R-squared 0.282' at the two ends |

Three grids, three escalating dress levels, one base rule set: each one adds exactly one
feature - first a shaded band, then a merged band - and never adds vertical rules or a full
frame. Nothing in the file is boxed.

## Caption template

Two dialects, and the seam is page 18/19:

- **pp5-18, bare number**: `Figure 1 Overview of Our Work`, `Table 1 Parameter List`,
  `Figure 2 Matching relation`, `Table 2 Estimation parameter interpretation`, `Table 3
  Regression results` - number, one space, noun phrase, no punctuation at all. 3-6 words.
- **pp19-21, colon**: `Figure 3: World Monetary Equilibrium`, `Figure 4: Market Share of
  Digital Currency in the United State (stable state)`, `Figure 5: ... (Imbalance state)` -
  number, colon, longer phrase, and in the two simulation plots a parenthesised condition
  naming the regime.

The colon arrives with the first pasted result and never leaves. Captions print BELOW on all
five numbered figures and ABOVE on all three grids - the split is figure-vs-table, not
style-vs-style. No caption carries a unit, a variable symbol, a parameter value or a
conclusion; the two parenthesised conditions are the only parameters anywhere in a caption.

## Context connectives

- **Nothing is ever named by number in prose.** The strings 'Figure 1' ... 'Figure 5' and
  'Table 1' ... 'Table 3' occur zero times outside their own captions.
- The pointer, when there is one, is a **deictic clause ending in a colon**: `The result is
  shown as figure below:` (Figure 3), `Other parameters' estimations are shown as follow:`
  (Table 2), `The results are as follows:` (Table 3). Lowercase 'figure', and the third one
  names nothing at all.
- Three exhibits get **no pointer**: Figure 1 follows a topic sentence, Figure 2 follows a set
  of equations, Figure 4 follows the sentence that already states its answer.
- Two get **no read-back either**: Table 1 and Figure 5 end their subsection, so the next line
  on the page is a heading.
- **The verdict comes first.** Figure 4 is introduced by `Through simulation, we find that the
  market share of digital currency will stabilize at about 65.21% regardless of the initial
  trading proportion.` - the chart is confirmation of a number the prose already gave. Figure 3
  is the same: the paragraph reports the 130-country outcome and only then says 'the result is
  shown as figure below'.
- **One sentence carries two figures**: `But when the supranational central bank loses its
  regulatory capacity, the market share of digital currency will decline rapidly, even lower
  than the initial share.` closes Figure 4 and opens Figure 5.

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **The printed footer disagrees with the file**: PDF page 5 prints `Page 3 of 24` while the
  file has 26 pages, because the two appendix pages were appended after the page count was
  fixed. Page-offset 2, total-offset 2.
- **The layout pass dates Table 1's overflow to the wrong section.** Section 3.1.1 is detected
  on p6, so the eleven parameter rows carried onto p6 read as belonging to "Digital Currencies:
  Price and Risk"; they belong to 2.2.
- **The appendix's numbered list items parse as numbered headings**, so the p25 plate's owner
  prints as `1.Total Trade Volume of the United State` - a list item, not a section.
- **Two prose columns on p4 were measured as regions**, both flagged `fragment_suspected`, both
  refused here as text.
- **The text layer destroys Table 1's notation**: `M d（ig M ）` and `V（d Vf）` are what the
  layer holds for `M_dig(M_flat)` and `V_d(V_f)`, so no quoted cell text from that grid can be
  trusted and none is quoted.

## Declared deficits

**None.** Every measured region on the twelve exhibit-bearing pages is either an exhibit row or
a documented refusal, Table 1's second half is accounted through `continued` rather than
dropped, and no caption in the detector's list lacks a row.
rules: A caption's punctuation is a running date stamp: the bare-number dialect runs pp5-18 and the colon dialect runs pp19-21, with no case either way outside its own span. [caption.numbering]

The dialect changes where the paper changes what it is doing - the last bare caption is the regression console, the first colon caption is the first pasted result image - so a caption's punctuation tracks the chapter's purpose, not the object's genus. [caption.numbering]
Captions sit BELOW all five figures and ABOVE all three grids; the side is decided by figure-vs-table and never varies within a class. [caption.position]

A condition belongs in the caption only when the exhibable varies by regime: the two simulation plots print '(stable state)' and '(Imbalance state)', and the three theoretical objects print no condition at all. [caption.conditions]
No caption in this paper carries a unit, a variable symbol, a parameter value or a conclusion; every caption is a bare noun phrase of three to six words. [caption.variable_count]
Nothing is named by number in prose - zero 'Figure N' or 'Table N' strings outside captions - so a figure that wants to be found is found by position, not by reference. [mention.count]
The pointer, where it exists, is a colon-ended deictic clause ('... are shown as follow:', '... is shown as figure below:'), never a numbered citation. [mention.lead_pattern]
A chart of a simulation is introduced by the verdict, not by the chart: the sentence before the caption already states the number, and the figure follows as confirmation. [mention.lead_sentence]
One sentence can close one exhibit and open the next; the transition between Figures 4 and 5 is a single line serving as read-back and lead-in at once. [mention.trail_sentence]

3-D is a response to a missing third variable, and this paper has none: the three drawings encode category, the three charts encode time, and the three grids hold text or coefficients. [geometry.three_d]

Category is drawn, magnitude is plotted: the three diagrams mark class by box position, box presence or fill colour, and every numeric axis in the file belongs to a chart of a simulation. [geometry.family]
The legend lives inside the frame whenever there is room: all three keyed exhibits put it inside, two in the upper right of a plot and one over empty ocean. [geometry.legend]
A wide categorical map needs a legend, a narrow time series does not: the choropleth keys four classes, the appendix fit plate keys nothing even though it plots two series. [geometry.legend]
No exhibit in the file carries a colourbar: the choropleth's four fills are keyed by a swatch list inside the map and the charts use marker shape instead of a ramp. [geometry.colorbar]

Grid dress escalates one feature at a time: Table 1 is plain booktabs, Table 2 adds shaded bands, Table 3 adds a merged summary band, and none of them adds a vertical rule or an outer frame. [table.rule_style]
Zebra shading marks membership, not parity: Table 2 bands the rows that belong to one parameter group, so the alternation is irregular by design. [table.zebra]
A merged band is how a console fits a summary under a wide header: Table 3 pushes 'Observations 53' and 'R-squared 0.282' to the two ends of one row that spans nine columns. [table.merged_cells]
A grid may break across a page rather than shrink: Table 1 prints its header once, opens p6 mid-row and carries eleven more parameters with no repeated header. [table.continued]
Numeric columns in a pasted console are centred, so decimals do not align and no grid in the file claims decimal alignment. [table.decimal_aligned]
Notes live inside the object, not under it: Table 3 prints 'Standard errors in parentheses' and the star legend below its own last rule but inside the pasted block. [table.note_sentence]

tables.note: six of the seventeen parameters, header printed once: a heavy rule above, a heavier rule under 'Parameter | Description', a thin rule between every pair of rows, no vertical rule and no side frames, so the stub column is held only by the whitespace of the indent. The grid is announced by nothing - it starts one blank line under the '2.2 Variable Description' heading, with no pointer sentence before it and no read-back after it - and it is not closed on p5: p6 opens mid-row at 'e' and carries the other eleven parameters with no repeated header, which is why the row here claims seven rows and `continued`.

tables.note: seven parameters against the method used to measure each, header 'Parameter | Estimation method', booktabs rules, and the paper's only shaded grid: light grey bands alternate down the seven data rows, not on a strict every-other rhythm but on the rows the authors judged to be one group ('pc_{f-o}', 'C'/'δ', 'p_{o-f}').
